profiles.meeting_scenario: A planning meeting at a U.S. multisite Alzheimer's clinical trial coordinating center for the INTERCEPT-AD phase 1a/b study of ACU193. The immediate context is that enrollment for the multiple ascending dose portion is about to begin, and the team needs to finalize how novel biomarker and safety assessments will be operationalized across sites without changing the approved protocol. The agenda is to align on the baseline visit workflow, what counts as the required 'early AD' confirmation package before randomization, how the digital cognitive battery and arterial spin labeling MRI will be scheduled, and who owns site-facing instructions. The expected outcome is a practical rollout plan for the first three sites, including visit sequencing, site guidance, and a near-term timeline for activation materials.

members.name: Dr. Elena Park
members.expertise: Neurology, early Alzheimer's trial design, biomarker strategy
members.background: A behavioral neurologist who has led sponsor-side planning for early-stage neurodegeneration programs and helped shape the ACU193 phase 1 biomarker package.
members.private_state: She wants the first sites activated quickly while preserving the scientific integrity of exploratory target-engagement and digital biomarker data, and she is particularly concerned that operational complexity will cause delays or inconsistent data capture.
hidden_assumptions: When the team says 'baseline,' it means the pre-dose anchor day for all efficacy and biomarker comparisons, even if some screening procedures were completed days earlier.
A 'PET-positive' participant can be confirmed using the subject's recent florbetapir scan from memory-clinic records if that scan already established amyloid positivity under local reading standards.

If the protocol says the digital battery is collected at baseline and follow-up, sites can administer it in clinic under supervised, standardized conditions unless a home component is explicitly required.
The site activation package is primarily an operational quick-start bundle for site coordinators, not a fully version-controlled imaging and vendor technical manual.
Safety review for dose escalation will be considered complete once the scheduled MRI read window and clinical review are done, even if a few exploratory biomarker uploads trail behind.

members.name: Rachel Kim
members.expertise: Multisite trial startup, vendor implementation, protocol operations
members.background: A clinical operations specialist who has run startup and execution for CNS trials involving central imaging vendors, eCOA platforms, and complex visit schedules across community and academic sites.
members.private_state: She wants to avoid preventable protocol deviations and site confusion, and she is especially worried that ambiguous instructions around imaging, prior records, and vendor workflows will create rework after sites are activated.
hidden_assumptions: When the team says 'baseline,' sites will interpret it as the entire pre-randomization visit package, including any assessments done during the screening window and carried forward if allowed.

A 'PET-positive' participant means positivity documented through the trial's designated source pathway, ideally with centrally collected imaging files or at minimum a sponsor-approved source package, not just a community report in the chart.
The digital battery is a vendor-managed remote assessment workflow with home practice, device provisioning rules, and timestamp requirements, even if the protocol only names the battery generally.
The site activation package must include enough detail for imaging, digital, and source-document handling to pass monitor review without local improvisation.
A cohort is not really ready for escalation review until all required safety-related data streams tied to the review packet are reconciled in the operational tracker.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree to 'capture the digital battery and ASL MRI at baseline.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means these assessments should be anchored to the pre-dose day used for comparison to on-treatment change, even if other screening items occur earlier.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means any allowed pre-randomization assessment obtained within the screening window can serve as the baseline data point if operationally designated that way.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In clinical trial planning, 'baseline' is a routine term that usually feels self-explanatory; because both are thinking about compliant pre-treatment data collection, the phrase creates false consensus and neither expects a hidden difference in temporal anchoring.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree that sites should only randomize participants once 'PET-positive' status is confirmed.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 thinks a recent florbetapir PET result from an outside memory clinic, documented in the medical record and clinically interpreted as amyloid-positive, is sufficient confirmation for enrollment planning unless a specific exception is raised.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 thinks confirmation requires collection through the study's expected source pathway, such as image transfer or a sponsor-approved documentation packet that can support centralized operational review before randomization.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both are aligned on the high-level requirement that subjects must be amyloid-positive, and the disagreement is only about the evidentiary threshold behind the same phrase, which feels too administrative to restate in a strategic planning conversation.

misalignment_points.topic: How the digital battery will be administered
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree to 'roll out the digital battery' at the first three sites.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 assumes sites can administer the computerized cognitive battery during scheduled clinic visits with coordinator supervision and standard site devices, using home completion only if a site prefers it.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 assumes the battery will follow the vendor's remote workflow, including device/account setup, home practice expectations, and centralized timestamp monitoring.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both believe they are discussing the same named assessment and neither sees administration mode as a first-order scientific decision; it sounds like an implementation detail that should already be implicit in the vendor setup.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree to send sites the 'site package' by next week.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means a concise startup bundle: visit schedule summary, safety reminders, biomarker timing table, and a coordinator-facing FAQ sufficient to begin training.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means a broader activation packet that also includes imaging transfer instructions, digital vendor workflows, source-document expectations for outside PET records, and escalation-review data handling notes.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The phrase 'site package' is common shorthand in startup work, and because each person routinely deals with a different layer of materials, both assume their fuller picture is the obvious default without listing every component.

turns.inner_thought: We need the first three MAD sites moving now, but I do not want the exploratory biomarker layer to become so complicated that startup stalls. For me, baseline has to mean the pre-dose anchor day; otherwise the digital and ASL data will be noisy for early signal interpretation. If we keep that anchor clean, we can tolerate some screening activity happening earlier.
turns.utterance: Thanks, everyone. The main goal today is to get the first three sites ready for the multiple ascending dose portion and lock the baseline workflow for biomarkers and safety so we can activate without creating avoidable churn.

turns.inner_thought: What we need this week is operational clarity: what has to be in place before randomization, how vendors are triggered, and what sits in the site package. Baseline will be whatever compliant pre-randomization assessments we designate within the screening window, but I do not need to say that because Elena is aligned on getting usable pre-treatment data. My bigger concern is that sites improvise if the package is too thin.
turns.utterance: That makes sense. From operations, the key decisions for this week are randomization readiness, the vendor handoffs, and getting the site package out on a timeline the first three sites can actually use.

turns.inner_thought: I want the digital battery and ASL MRI tied to the pre-dose day so we can compare on-treatment change against a single anchor. The digital battery can be done in clinic under supervision; that is the simplest way to keep performance conditions standardized. If we say baseline and roll out the digital battery, that should be straightforward enough without opening a debate about delivery mode.
turns.utterance: For the clinical piece, I'd like us to capture the digital battery and ASL MRI at baseline so we have a clean anchor for the early readouts, and we should roll out the digital battery at the first three sites rather than staggering it later.

turns.inner_thought: Baseline should be manageable if sites can complete pieces anywhere in the screening window and carry forward what is allowed; that is how they will operationalize it. On the digital side, roll out the digital battery means the vendor's remote workflow has to be live from the start, including accounts, timestamps, and practice steps. I assume Elena just wants it active and available, not to redesign the workflow.
turns.utterance: I think that's workable. We can keep baseline manageable within the screening window, and I'll align the digital battery rollout with the vendor's existing setup for the first sites so they're not building from scratch.

turns.inner_thought: Eligibility is the next pressure point. If someone already has a recent florbetapir scan in the chart from a memory clinic showing amyloid positivity, that should be enough to keep enrollment moving unless there is a specific issue. I do not want sites waiting for unnecessary administrative steps once PET-positive status is confirmed.
turns.utterance: On eligibility, I want sites moving as soon as PET-positive status is confirmed, especially for patients who have already been worked up in memory clinics and are otherwise ready to go.

turns.inner_thought: Agreed in principle, but sites should only randomize once PET-positive status is confirmed through the study's source pathway. At minimum I need a sponsor-acceptable documentation package before randomization, ideally with image transfer supportable for review. I'll put that into the startup materials and coordinators will know what to collect.
turns.utterance: Agreed. I'll make sure coordinators have instructions for collecting the PET-positive confirmation into the startup materials before randomization so that part is handled consistently.

turns.inner_thought: Infusion days are already busy, so I do not want to overload sites with extra cognitive procedures beyond what matters. As long as the digital battery is in the plan, we can keep the rest of the cognitive workup streamlined on dosing visits. In my mind that means coordinators can run the battery efficiently in clinic when scheduled.
turns.utterance: Good. And to keep burden down, I'm comfortable if sites keep the cognitive testing streamlined on infusion-day visits as long as the digital battery is in the plan.

turns.inner_thought: That works if I sequence the vendor workflow correctly. The devices, accounts, and home steps need to be set up before those visits or the timestamps will become a mess. Elena is focused on keeping visits light, which is fine; I'll just make sure the digital battery is live in time through the remote pathway.
turns.utterance: That works from my side. I'll sequence the device and account steps so the digital battery is live before subjects reach those visits.

turns.inner_thought: Now I need something practical for activation, not a giant manual that delays us. A concise site package with the visit schedule, baseline timing table, and key safety reminders should be enough to start training coordinators and open sites. If Rachel keeps it tight, we can avoid startup drag.
turns.utterance: Then what I'd like by next week is a concise site package with the visit schedule, the baseline timing table, and the key safety reminders so we don't slow activation.

turns.inner_thought: Next week is feasible, but the site package needs to be broad enough that monitors and coordinators are not left guessing. I need imaging handling, digital workflow details, source expectations for prior amyloid PET documentation, and escalation-review data handling included. If we omit those, we'll pay for it after activation.
turns.utterance: Next week is feasible. I'll make sure the site package also covers imaging handling, digital workflow details, and source expectations for prior amyloid PET documentation so the sites have what they need up front.

turns.inner_thought: That's fine as long as it does not become unwieldy. What matters for the first cohorts is interpretable baseline and timely safety review for dose escalation. I can live with a few exploratory uploads trailing if the scheduled MRI read and clinical review are done; startup should not be overengineered.
turns.utterance: Exactly. For the first cohorts, the priority is interpretable baseline and clean safety data for the go/no-go decisions, without overcomplicating startup for the sites.

turns.inner_thought: I need to leave this meeting with ownership clear: startup materials on me, vendor coordination on me, and a concrete activation plan for the first three sites. I still need all safety-related data streams reconciled in the operational tracker before I consider an escalation packet truly ready, but that is an execution detail I can manage through the materials and tracker.
turns.utterance: Perfect. I'll take the lead on the startup materials and vendor coordination, and I'll circulate the activation plan for the first three sites with owners and timing so we can keep this moving.
